messages:
Anna Li: Heads-up — I pushed an RBAC change to privacypath that restricts the 'dsar-delete' action to the service principal only. This may block the nightly DSAR deletion job. I'll roll back in 10m if there's a problem. :eyes:
Mike Patel: Which binding did you remove? is it the data-ops group or the job SA?
Anna Li: removed data-ops from role privacypath.delete. Command I ran:```bash
# remove binding
gcloud iam roles remove-iam-policy-binding privacypath.delete \
  --member="group:data-ops@redwood.com"```
Deploybot: deploybot: rollout started: iam-policy-update-privacypath by anna.li at 2024-11-02T23:12Z :rocket:
Sara Gomez: If the job loses access we might see KMS errors too. Deletion flow needs KMS decrypt to validate tombstones before remove — remember we rotated the key yesterday.
Jordan Reed: Pause the deletion queue until we confirm. We can't risk partial deletes during a retention/DSAR window. I'll open a quick triage.
Mike Patel: @Anna can you re-add data-ops temporarily? I can run a backfill and capture audit logs for any failed attempts.
Anna Li: done — re-added data-ops binding. Command:```bash
gcloud iam roles add-iam-policy-binding privacypath.delete \
  --member="group:data-ops@redwood.com"```
Ops note: after re-add, I saw the DSAR job still fail once with KMS error: sample from audit.log:```text
2024-11-02T23:22:10Z uid=svc-dsar-job action=delete object=embeddings/abc123 err="AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt"````
Sara Gomez: That matches the rotation hypothesis — the job SA lost decrypt perms on the key. The key policy shows a rotation principal change: `kms:members` removed `svc-dsar-job@redwood.com`.
Legal Bot: quick reminder: we have 2 active DSARs pending deletion this week (case #2024-558 and #2024-559). If we need to pause, flag as legal-hold. Do not drop evidence while we triage.
Jordan Reed: Opening incident inc-privacypath-1717773333 and tagging sec/infra/legal. Triage note: RBAC change + KMS rotation combined to produce DSAR deletion failures. Potential risk: malicious RBAC changes could be used to block deletions or hide artifacts.
Mike Patel: Running safe backfill now (read-only pass + log export). Will not modify records until we confirm legal holds. Progress: scanning objects... ETA ~7m.
Anna Li: I'll also add a small runbook note to the RBAC playbook about 'privacypath.delete' -> KMS interaction. We should require a preflight check for key ACLs before rolling RBAC changes.
Sara Gomez: For retention exceptions, we'll tag items with `retention:exception` and exclude them from purge. Ops: please ensure audit retention for DSAR events is extended to 7 years for compliance evidence.
Mike Patel: Backfill done. Summary: 42 deletions attempted, 39 succeeded after re-add, 3 skipped due to `retention:exception`. Export snippet:```json
[{"obj":"embeddings/abc123","status":"skipped","reason":"retention:exception"}, {"obj":"embeddings/def456","status":"deleted"}]```
Jordan Reed: Action items assigned: 1) Mike: publish backfill audit and export to legal 2) Anna: add RBAC+KMS preflight to playbook 3) Sara: confirm KMS rotation change docs and restore svc-dsar-job decrypt acl 4) I will run a short vuln triage and assign remediation if this pattern is exploitable.
Anna Li: ACL restored for svc-dsar-job on KMS. I also pushed a rollback-pressure check to our CI: it tests `kms:Decrypt` + role bindings before applying changes.
Deploybot: deploybot: iam-policy-update-privacypath rollout completed at 2024-11-02T23:58Z by anna.li :white_check_mark:
Legal Bot: Received audit export, storing in secure evidence bucket. Confirmed both DSAR cases are preserved.
Jordan Reed: Closing incident, adding postmortem note: root cause = coordinated RBAC + KMS rotation without cross-check. Recommendations: preflight checks, update change-review checklist (include legal when DSAR window active), and extended audit retention.
Anna Li: will add the runbook PR today. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
